sentences.text: Heard Shri Ranjan Krishna Pandey, learned counsel for the accused/applicant, Shri Virendra Kumar Maurya, learned A.G.A. for the State-respondent and perused the record.
Learned counsel for the accused applicant submitted that the accused applicant is innocent and has falsely been implicated in the crime.
The victim is a contesting party.
She willingly went with the accused applicant and they both got married.
He further submitted that the victim has not supported the prosecution version in her statements recorded under Sections 161 & 164 Cr.P.C.

sentences.text: He further submitted that the accused applicant is languishing in jail since 07.07.2022 and he has no criminal history as stated in para 19 of the affidavit filed in support of the bail application.
Hence the applicant should be enlarged on bail.
Learned A.G.A. appearing on behalf of the State opposed the bail application of the accused/applicant and submitted that as per the educational certificate, the victim is a minor girl.
Her consent being minor has no meaning in the eyes of law.
Hence, the applicant should not be enlarged on bail.
Considered the rival submissions made by the parties' counsel and perused the material available on record.
It transpires from the record that the victim has not supported the case of prosecution in her statement recorded under Sections 161 & 164 Cr.P.C.
As per the ossification test report, her age has been found about 18 years.
Considering all the fact and circumstances of the case as mentioned above, without commenting on merits of the case, it appears just to enlarge the accused applicant on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application filed on behalf of applicant is allowed.

Let the applicantNaukhe Lal involved in Case Crime No.258 of 2022 (supra) be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions;
(i) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.

In case of default of this condition,
it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed, either personally or through his counsel.
In case of his absence, without sufficient cause, the trial court may proceed against his under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iii) In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. is issued and the applicant fails to appear before the court on the date fixed in such proclamation, then, the trial court shall initiate proceedings against his, in accordance with law, under Section 174-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iv) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for (i)
opening of the case, (ii) framing of charge and (iii) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the trial court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause,
then it shall be open for the trial court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against his in accordance with law.
